13. In the circumstances, in order to avoid delay and reduce business costs, so that the price of product goods does not escalate due to delay, in the process of transportation and monopoly created by the BCVOA and COAB, the petitioners themselves purchased several lighterage vessels for transportation of their respective imported goods from the mother vessel to their respective factory premises. All the vessels are registered with the relevant government departments with necessary permits, which are being used by the petitioners for exclusively transporting their respective imported goods from mother vessels. The vessels purchased by the petitioners work as a backward linkage service for exclusively serving the riverine transport needs of the petitioners which save undue harassment and delay in transporting raw materials. 

 21. The Director-General of Shipping (DG Shipping) as respondent No.5 has filed affidavits-in-opposition in writ petition No. 7302 of 2021 and 10935 of 2014. Contentions of the respondent in both Rules, inter alia, are that the DG Shipping as the appropriate authority, is empowered to formulate policy from time to time subject to approval of the Government. The policy in question was adopted under the direction of the Government i.e Ministry of Shipping. The policy was accepted by the members of the committee unanimously in a legit and reasonable background of making a level playing field in the water transport sector commuting from Chattogram Port, carrying goods from mother vessels. 

 22. The DG Shipping is responsible for inland water transport and shipping administration of all inland ships and for formulating policies and directives (11-1691t) relating to the shipping and welfare for the maritime sector. According to the Rules of business, 1996 as amended in 2012, schedule 1(36), Ministry of Shipping instructed all regulatory bodies to perform their respective duties. The Government i.e respondent No.1 vide its office order dated 21-4-2013 instructed and directed the DG Shipping to prepare a policy and also to form a committee comprising 12 representatives from each stakeholder regarding this matter. The same was approved and respondent No.1 i.e Ministry of Shipping directed the DG Shipping to take necessary action to implement the same vide its letter dated 19-6-2013. The policy (নীতিমালা) cannot be impugned at all, inasmuch as the same has been framed by a lawful authority. The aforesaid policy was adopted unanimously with the participation of all stakeholders for public interest in order to bring discipline and smooth operation of discharging goods from mother vessels. 

 24. From the official documents (Annexure-1 and 2) it is clear that the DG Shipping has been duly authorized by the Government to formulate and adopt such policy. Not only that, the Government in most democratic way formed a committee comprising 12 representative from concerned government bodies and other stakeholders like ship owners, so that a balanced policy could be formulated. Furthermore, the committee in their meeting dated 20-4-2013 reached into an agreement making the following clause: 

 A. The Nitimala, 2013 as a whole itself, on the face of it, appears to be a draft copy without having any reference to the issuing authority at its beginning and top. It looks like a memorandum of understanding (MoU) among certain private persons (representatives of trade organization) and government officials and so it can, at best, be enforcible among those signatories as an MoU. 

 40. In support of submissions, the learned Advocates refer to the cases of Bangladesh vs Shafiuddin and others reported in 50 DLR (AD) 27 and the case of Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh vs Md Habibur Rahman Manu reported in 31 DLR (AD) 152 and the case of Bangladesh Bank vs East West Property Developments (pot) Limited and others reproted in 69 DLR (AD) 294. 

 42. In reply, Mr Sheikh Mohammad Murshed, the learned Additional Attorney-General (Addl. AG) contends that it is not an independent Nitimala but a Nitimala embodied with a memorandum of understanding executed by all the stakeholders involved in the lighterage vessel business. Some of the petitioners are party to the said memorandum and subsequent addendum of the memorandum. As such, they cannot challenge the said memorandum. He further contends that the contents of the Nitimala clearly indicate that it was framed at the Government decision with the consent of the relevant stakeholders. Referring to Clauses 12.9 and 12.11 of the Nitimala, he also contends that in order to bring discipline in the marine routes and to break the monopoly business of a vested quarter, the Nitimala has been introduced by the Government having its legal authority. 

 43. Adopting the contentious of learned Addl. AG, Mr Probir Neogi, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the WTC in all the writ petitions further contends that Department of Shipping is a part and parcel of the Government as per section 4 of the Merchant Shipping Ordinance, 1983 and, as such, the Nitimala under the signature of DG shipping is tantamount to have been framed by the Government in accordance with law. 

 52. Premble of the ISO, 1976 provides that it has been enacted for the survey, registration and control of navigation of vessels plying on inland waters. The Inland Water Transport Authority Ordinance, 1958 (BIWTA Ordinance, 1958) has also been enacted for development, maintenance and control of inland water transport and of certain inland navigable waterways. 

 “সমুদ্র পরিবহন অধিদপ্তরের নিবন্ধিত লাইটার জাহাজযোগে বাংলাদেশের সমুদ্র বন্দরসমূহে পণ্য পরিবহন সংক্রান্ত নীতিমালা-২০১৩”i.e the name of the Nitimala has been provided here. But admittedly, the petitioners' vessels are not “সমুদ্র পরিবহন অধিদপ্তরের নিবন্ধিত জাহাজ”as they are registered with the office of Registrar under the ISO, 1976. Further, we do not find here any reference as to the office of framer of this Nitimala and under what authority it has been framed. At the last page of the Nitimala, it appears that the ministry of shipping constituted a 12 member committee on 21-4-2013 who by their 3 (three) meetings prepared the draft Nitimala. Out of 12 (twelve) members of the committee, 11 (eleven) members put their signatures amongst whom there are some private persons introducing themselves as representatives of different trade bodies along with four government officials on behalf of the BIWTA, Ministry of Shipping, Chattogram Port Authority and Department of Shipping. At the bottom of the Nitimala, the DG Shipping put his signature. Before the signatures of the aforementioned members, the conclusion of the Nitimala is as follows: 

 63. Learned Addl. AG although has drawn our attention to certain provisions of the Bagladesh Marchant Shipping Ordinance, 1983, shortly, the BMS Ordinance, 1983 (parent law) and from those provisions, we find that by this Ordinance (statute of parliament), the power has been delegated to the Government to make rules or regulation in relation to certain provisions of certain chapter of the BMS Ordinances, 1983. But in respect of this particular Nitimala, the respondents could not show or assert any such source of delegated authority for framing this Nitimala. It is to be noted here that within the 4th corner of the purported Nitimala, there is no relfection that the Ministry of Shipping framed this Nitimala. Only DG Shipping is the signatory in the Nitimala. 

 64. By another attempt, referring to section 4 of the BMS Ordinance, 1983 Mr Neogi submits that DG, Shipping is the part and parcel of the Government and that DG Shipping as the Government having the authority framed the Nitimala in question with the consent of the relevant stakeholders and so, to consider his submission, we have gone through section 4 of the BMS Ordinance, 1983 which runs as follows: 

 "4. (1) The Government may, for efficient administration of this Ordinance, establish a Department of Shipping which shall be headed by a Director-General of Shipping. 

 (3) The Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, direct that the powers exercisable by it under any of the provisions of this Ordinance specified in the notification shall, subject to such conditions, if any, as may be so specified, be exercisable also by the Director-General of Shipping. 

 Provided that no such order shall be made without the previous approval of the Government if it relates to any of the powers of the Government which the Director-General of Shipping has been authorized to exercise under sub-section (3)." 

 65. On a plain reading of the provisions, it appears that the Government has established the Department of Shipping headed by the DG Shipping and so it is clear that the DG Shipping himself is appointed by the Government in accordance with subsection (1) of section 4 and, as such, there is no scope to treat him as the Government. Further, subsection (3) of the said provision makes it more clear that the Government by notification in official gazette can direct that the power exercisable by it under this Ordinance may be exercised by the DG Shipping. But that has to be specified in the gazetted notification and that the respondents could not show us any such gazette that DG Shipping has got authority from the Government under this provision. In other words, here, the respondents have failed to show that in accordance with section 4 of the BMS Ordinances, 1983, the Government by gazette notification has delegated any power to the DG Shipping in order to frame the Nitimala in question. Therefore, even considering the section 4 of the BMS Ordinances, 1983, we cannot accept the submission of the learned Advocates for the respondents that DG Shipping has got the authority/power to frame such Nitimala. 

 66. Mr Neogi refers to a case reported in 47 DLR (AD) I that mere omission to mention the source of power will not invalidate the law. But here the Nitimala does not show expressly or impliedly, the source of power for its framing and even learned Addl. AG and Mr Neogi, on behalf of respondents could not show any source of power referring to any other papers that any authority has been given by the Government through gazette notification to the DG to make such Nitimala. As such, the cited case reported in 47 DLR (AD) I is not applicable in this case. 

 69. 2nd fold submission of learned Addl. AG is, by the Annexure-1 and 2 to the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the DG Shipping in writ petition No. 7302 of 2021, the Government has delegated the power to the DG Shipping for framing the Nitimala in question. We have gone through both the Annexures. But on a careful reading of the aforesaid correspondences, we find that by Annexure-1 (memo dated 21-4-2013) a monitoring cell was constituted and that Annexure-2 (memo dated 19-6-2013) also does not delegate any power to the DG for framing the Nitimala in question. 

 70. Above all, these annexures are not the notifications in the official gazette as per requirement of section 4(3) of the Ordinances, 1983. Precisely, there is no Gazette Notification from the Government delegating power to the DG Shipping for framing Nitimala in question in accordance with the requirement of section 4(3) of the BMS Ordinance, 1983. 

 78. To appreciate the submissions, we have gone through the records and the relevant papers regarding the WTC from which it appears that in the year 2005, a tripartite understanding was signed by the Chattogram Chamber of Commerce and Industries (CCCI), the Coastal Ship Owners Association of Bangladesh (COAB) and the Bangladesh Cargo Vessel Owners Association (BCVOA). These three private trade bodies, in fact, initally introduced themselves jointly as Water Transport Coordination Cell (WTCC). But subsequently, the Chattogram Chamber of Commerce and Industries left the Agreement and on 12-6-2009 another bilateral memorandum of understanding was executed between the COAB and the BCVOA. It is also admitted that there is no such separate organization either privately or under the supervision of the Government in the name of WTC although the WTC has been referred to in different correspondences of the Government as well as in the Nitimala in question. Albeit, in some clauses of the Nitimala in question, activities of WTC are mentioned but in the impugned Nitimala, 2013, we do not find any clause constituting the WTC, as Mr Neogi claims. Moreover, by the impugned circular dated 23-8-2021 of the writ petitions, the Department of Shipping required the lighterage vessel owners to take serial from WTC for loading/unloading of the vessels and even clause 12.9 of the Nitimala in question requires the private vessel owners to carry part of their imported cargoes by the vessels controlled by the WTC instead of their own vessels infringing their fundamental rights. Even WTC is fixing and controlling fare of vessels which cannot be done by such private association. 

 79. The submission of the petitioners are that basically WTC is a joint agreement of two private organizations of vessel owners who are trying to make the business monopoly by taking under their control using the Nitimala in question in connivance with the Government officials. We find from a number of clauses of the Nitimala in question and the circular dated 23-8-2021 (Annexure-D) that WTC has been assigned to control all the private vessels. An owner of a private vessel has the right to use his vessel at his own way and of course, he has to follow discipline and laws/rules within the marine route, in particular, with in port area in discharging loading/unloading of the imported cargoes. But to maintain discipline and law/rules two private trade bodies having similar interest' and status in operation of vessels, cannot be entrusted for controlling other vessels.

Further, from preamble of the Inland Shipping Ordinance (ISO), 1976 we find that it has been enacted for the purpose of survey, registration and control of navigation of vessels plying on inland waters. Accordingly, all the vessels of petitioners are registered and controlled under the ISO, 1976. Therefore, by passing this statutory authority, WTC cannot run in the name of maintaining disclipine on the waterways of the country. Hence, (byeond the port area), the vessels shall be controlled within the waterways of Bangldesh under the Inland Shipping Ordinance, 1976 (ISO, 1976), the Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority Ordinance, 1958 (B1WTA Ordinance, 1958).
